title: Stale role provisioning during SAML nested-group sync leading to temporary admin over-privilege and missing revoke audit events
creator: Avery Cho
description: A production customer reported that during an org migration their user briefly gained admin-level privileges while another user lost access. Root cause: a race between the incremental SAML nested-group sync job and the session token role-binding path. The incremental sync applied a group add, provisioning an elevated role in RBAC v2, while the subsequent group removal (part of a consolidation) was processed in a separate batch that failed to emit role_revoked audit events for active sessions. The issue is a combination of stale provisioning state, session token binding semantics, and an intermittent audit-logger backpressure that dropped revoke events. This ticket tracks investigation, live mitigation, code fixes, and follow-ups.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure SAML IdP with nested groups: org-admins -> team-leads -> eng-team.
2) Trigger incremental group sync that only sends deltas (add team-leads for user X).
3) Simultaneously run a separate consolidation job that removes the upstream group for user X before the second sync completes.
4) Create an active session for user X prior to the consolidation and observe role bindings on the session token.
5) Revoke or remove group membership; confirm that RBAC state does not emit role_revoked for the active session and that the UI still shows elevated permissions until session refresh.
6) Observe audit-events dashboard for missing revoke events in the time window 2025-02-10 02:00-03:00 UTC.

2025-02-10 03:25 UTC - Triage call with SRE, Security Eng, and Customer Success. Assigned ENG-48921 to Security Eng.
2025-02-10 04:00 UTC - Reproduced locally with a multi-stage sync harness (steps above). Observed session token contained stale_role_claims header.
2025-02-10 06:45 UTC - Correlated missing role_revoked events with audit-logger metrics: write-errors increased during consolidation window (backpressure from ES bulk indexing).

2025-02-11 09:20 UTC - Verified SAML assertion attribute precedence: nested group membership expansion returns both parent and child groups; delta sync logic applied parent add first, then child remove in separate job.

2025-02-12 11:30 UTC - Decision: ship a targeted hotfix to prevent provisioning on partial sync when session token binding is pending; also patch audit-logger retry paths. Longer-term: refactor session rebind flow to be idempotent and emit compensating events on mismatch.
2025-02-14 16:05 UTC - Security review completed (see Confluence), code approved by @melissa.k and @omar-h. PR merged and deployed to staging.

https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6290 - audit-logger: add durable retry and compensating event emit on write failure
resolution_summary: Deployed a two-part fix: 1) short-term: incremental-provisioning now checks for active session token binding and defers provisioning until session rebind completes (avoids transient over-privilege), 2) audit-logger got improved retry/backoff and a compensating-emitter that writes synthetic role_revoked events when a write fails. We notified affected customers and provided remediation steps (force session refresh or rotate tokens). Post-deploy validation shows no missing revoke events in the 72h window and a single customer confirmed resolution.
rollout_plan: stage1: deploy hotfix to canary clusters (2025-02-16) and run synthetic SAML delta tests
stage2: promote to 30% of prod traffic and monitor audit-event drops and role binding diffs (48h)
stage3: full rollout and notify CS teams to close escalations
acceptance_criteria: No missing role_revoked events in synthetic replay for delta sync scenarios (verified on staging)
Active sessions reflect correct least-privilege within 60s of IdP group change or explicit session refresh
Metrics: audit-logger write_error rate <= baseline and retry success >= 99.9%
Customer confirmation from affected org that access anomalies are resolved
implementation_notes: Guard added in SyncWorker: if delta contains both add and delete for overlapping nested groups and sessionRebindPending(user) == true, enqueue a deferred job with 'rebind-wait' TTL=120s.
Audit-logger: move ES writes to a durable write-queue with exponential backoff and emit compensating 'audit:role_revoked:synthetic' events with original request metadata when final write fails.
Added unit tests for nested-group delta ordering and end-to-end integration test covering active session rebind and revoke event emission.

Tradeoff: deferring provisioning for up to 120s can delay legitimate grants (risk: short-lived delay) but reduces risk of transient over-privilege and gives time for consolidation jobs to settle. Long-term aim is immediate idempotent session rebind instead of deferral.
followups: ENG-49702 - Refactor session rebind to be idempotent and to patch session token in-place rather than requiring full refresh
ENG-50011 - Add per-org sync sequencing guarantees to prevent overlapping delta jobs for the same identity
SEC-312 - Run threat assessment on compensating-event semantics and ensure audit integrity for compliance customers
